content: Indication-specific dosing for red raspberry (Rubus idaeus, Rubus strigosus) leaf includes the following recommendations: For preparation, 5 grams of raspberry leaves are steeped in 150 mL of water. Alternatively, 4-8 mL of a liquid preparation can be taken orally three times daily (TID). Another option is a 1:1 tincture in 25% alcohol. For tea, 2 grams of dried raspberry leaf can be steeped in 240 mL of water. Therapeutic uses include: Cardiovascular disorders Diarrhea Dysmenorrhea (painful menstruation) Gastrointestinal disorders Support during labor and delivery Menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding) Prevention of miscarriage Morning sickness Topical treatment for inflammation of the mouth, throat, or skin Respiratory disorders Clinical evidence suggests little benefit compared to placebo. Adverse effects: None reported. Contraindications: Breast cancer Endometriosis Hormone-sensitive conditions Ovarian cancer Uterine cancer Uterine fibroids Pregnancy: Classified as Pregnancy Category A. An Australian study demonstrated no adverse outcomes associated with the use of raspberry leaf during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Lactation: No data available. Cost information: Not specified.
